# Acknowledgements {.unnumbered}

This book exists because drilling and completions reports capture far
more than operational summaries. Behind short entries such as "POOH to
change BHA due to erratic torque" sit decisions, experience, and
operational context that are obvious to the engineers involved in the
operation but invisible to standard AI systems that have never seen
field data.

This work depends on the global open-source community, whose open
models, software, and shared research make it possible to run powerful
AI tools locally and securely on a standard work laptop, without
sending proprietary data to the cloud.

Finally, thanks to every drilling, completions, and operations engineer
working through this material. You do not need to be a software
developer or data scientist to apply these methods. If you find an
error, test a method on your operational data that yields unexpected
results, or find a section that assumes too much technical background,
please reach out via the book's companion website. Feedback from
practitioners in the field is what keeps a guide like this practical
and honest.

The engineering direction, domain interpretation, educational approach,
and final technical decisions are the author's. AI tools, including
Claude, were used throughout the project to assist with drafting,
editing, documentation, and technical verification. All AI-assisted
work was reviewed and validated against actual operational datasets and
repeatable workflows. Responsibility for the final content remains with
the author.
